verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The kind 'missing-heading' is factually wrong. I rendered page 578 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v578/spec_p578.png) and read the printed glyphs. The page carries exactly one heading, set in bold: '14.6.13.1.2 Normal completion of a declarative procedure' (printed page 548, footer '548 (C)ISO/IEC 2023'). specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 24190 transcribes it verbatim - same clause number, same title, same word order, no dropped or altered token - and additionally carries the structural anchor '' on line 24189. The body text under it ('A declarative procedure is said to complete normally if...' and enumerated item 1) is also present and faithful. There is no lost PDF content on this page. (2) THE ONLY DIFFERENCE IS MARKDOWN HEADING DEPTH, WHICH IS FORMATTING, NOT CONTENT. The PDF has no '#' levels at all; ISO encodes hierarchy solely in the dotted clause number, and that number - 14.6.13.1.2 - is transcribed exactly. Typographically the PDF gives no basis for the claim's asserted depth: 14.6.13.1.1, 14.6.13.1.2 and 14.6.13.1.3 are all set in the identical bold run-in clause-heading style, with no visual level distinction between them. The '##' vs '####' choice is an artifact of the transcription's own markup convention and changes no meaning, no rule, and no derivable behavior. (3) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES ITS OWN PREMISE. It asserts the sibling 14.6.13.1.1 'General' is transcribed at '####'. In fact 14.6.13.1.1 'General' appears TWICE in the file - at '##' (line 24107) and at '####' (line 24148) - so the cited '####' is not the convention, merely one of two conflicting instances. The actual sibling set is mixed: 14.6.13.1.2 (24190) and 14.6.13.1.3 (24206) are at '##'; 14.6.13.1.4 (24240), 14.6.13.1.5 (24253) and 14.6.13.1.6 (24289) are at '###'; the fourth-level 14.6.13.2 (24548) and 14.6.13.3 (24593) are also at '##'. Heading depth is arbitrary throughout this whole region, so the '##' on 14.6.13.1.2 is neither anomalous nor attributable to page 578. (4) BOTH CITED LINE NUMBERS ARE WRONG, each by three. The heading is at line 24190, not 24187. Line 24145 is '### 14.6.13.1 Exception conditions', not the '#### 14.6.13.1.1 General' the claim attributes to it (that is line 24148). Rejected under the stated criteria: the 'missing' text is actually present, and the residual difference is formatting only.
verdict.corrected_description: No page-578 discrepancy. The heading '14.6.13.1.2 Normal completion of a declarative procedure' - the only heading printed on PDF page 578 (printed page 548) - is transcribed verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 24190 with its anchor and full body text. The claim's real content is a markdown heading-depth inconsistency, which is transcription formatting rather than PDF content, and it is not localized to page 578: heading depth across the entire 14.6.13.1.x family is arbitrary ('##' for .1.2/.1.3, '###' for .1.4/.1.5/.1.6, both '##' and '####' for two separate copies of .1.1). Out of scope but worth a separate ledger entry: lines 24086-24107 and 24127-24148 are a DUPLICATED heading block (14.6.12 / 14.6.13 / 14.6.13.1 / 14.6.13.1.1 'General' each emitted twice, at differing depths), which is a structural transcription defect on pages 576-577, not 578, and is a materially different finding from the one claimed.
